template.title: CAREER: HIGH-RESOLUTION NMR FOR PARAMAGNETIC SODIUM

section.title: ELECTRODES

question.text: Battery material samples will be synthesized in powder form and identified through a consistent and

json.answer: systematic labeling procedure, which will include sample composition, name of researcher and date.

section.title: Experimental data generated over the course of the research will include synthesis procedures and

question.text: results from characterization of battery electrode samples. Digital characterization data in tabular

json.answer: form will be produced by electrochemical testing, X-ray diffraction, solid-state NMR spectroscopy,

section.title: EPR spectroscopy, magnetometry, impedance spectroscopy, X-ray photoelectron and absorption

question.text: spectroscopy, and Mössbauer spectroscopy measurements. Rietveld refinements of scattering data

json.answer: will generate crystallographic data. Scanning electron microscopy will generate images. Synthetic

section.title: work and optimization of NMR experimental procedures will be documented in lab notebooks and

question.text: generate physical data. The Van der Ven group’s CASM software will be extended to enable the

json.answer: simulation of finite temperature NMR spectra of paramagnetic materials. First principles and Monte

section.title: Carlo simulations will produce text files, density of states plots and two-dimensional charge density

question.text: maps. Educational and outreach materials, and assessment results, will be digitized.

section.title: Data Format Standards

question.text: Data Format Standards

json.answer: In order to allow for interoperability, reproducibility, and reuse, all data will be stored and saved in

question.text: standard and open formats. Experimental characterization data will be stored and saved as, e.g.,

json.answer: ASCII, CSV, Word, Matlab and Python files. Microscope images will be stored as portable graphic

section.title: files (.tif, .jpg or .png format). Crystallographic data will be reported in standard crystallographic

question.text: information framework (*.cif) format to facilitate visualization and further analysis through widely

json.answer: available software tools (VESTA, cif2file, etc.). Crystallographic data for previously-unreported

section.title: compounds/structures will be uploaded to the ICSD database. First principles simulation input and

question.text: output files (generated with the VASP and CRYSTAL codes) will be stored as rich text format (*.rtf)

json.answer: files for readability across many programs and platforms. The CRYSTAL code manual will be

section.title: provided along CRYSTAL input/output data to allow for interpretation of variables. Both

question.text: CRYSTAL and VASP manuals are also available online. The Van der Ven group's CASM software

json.answer: currently interfaces with VASP, automates the construction of effective Hamiltonians and subjects

section.title: them to Monte Carlo simulations. CASM organizes all the files associated with VASP calculations

question.text: into a standard structure that can be accessed by subsequent runs of CASM, either by the same user

json.answer: or by a new user. A similar CASM interface and infrastructure will be developed here for

section.title: CRYSTAL calculations of NMR properties. The uniform file structure enforced by CASM for the

question.text: effective Hamiltonian construction and the large number of Monte Carlo simulations that are

json.answer: necessary to construct, e.g., temperature composition phase diagrams, will be extended to include

section.title: Fermi contact shifts and electric field gradient tensors. This will ensure that results from calculations

question.text: performed by different users are in a format that is readily accessible, either by CASM or directly by

json.answer: different people.

section.title: Access and sharing

question.text: The Program Toolkit and Activity Plans developed for the educational and outreach activities in

json.answer: partnership with Jamboree Housing (JH) will be uploaded to JH’s filesharing system for broad and

section.title: free dissemination to their different centers and partners in California. All of the research results will

question.text: be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications, conference presentations, and annual reports.

json.answer: The supporting information accompanying publications will include detailed

section.title: experimental/simulation/synthetic procedures, as well as detailed information on models used for

question.text: data analysis. All of the journals of interest to the group make supporting information files publicly-

json.answer: available online free of charge. In addition, all publication pre-prints will be made freely available,

section.title: along with supplementary information, on the UC eScholarship website.

question.text: Over the course of the project, digital data will be internally stored and shared for collaborative work

json.answer: on the UCSB-administered, Box platform with unlimited cloud storage. The privacy, security and

section.title: intellectual property protection of data stored in this manner are guaranteed by the privacy policy

question.text: and terms of service contract between University of California and Box. As a means of making data

json.answer: accessible and searchable, data collected over the course of this project will be stored in the data

section.title: repository Dryad. enables easy data upload and description, and creates digital object

question.text: identifiers (DOIs) for each dataset to help manage long-term data sharing through digital

json.answer: organization. We note that CASM systematically organizes all first-principles calculations that have

section.title: been performed on a given system and has tools to query a wide range of properties for each

question.text: calculation. Furthermore, any structure with a chemical ordering, magnetic ordering or a structural

json.answer: distortion that has been made "by hand" can be imported in a CASM project and made to be

section.title: consistent with the automatically enumerated configurations. Hence, for each system of interest to

question.text: this work, a structured CASM results packet that can easily be queried will be created (consisting of

json.answer: the results of electronic structure calculations, effective Hamiltonian interaction parameters and basis

section.title: functions and Monte Carlo results) and uploaded to Dryad. is free of charge for UCSB

question.text: researchers and can be accessed using a personal ORCID.

json.answer: CASM is an open source software package released under the GNU Lesser General Public License

section.title: (LGPL) and available free of charge via the prisms-center conda channel at

question.text: https://anaconda.org/prisms-center. All additions of the CASM software developed during this

json.answer: project will be incorporated into the CASM software and made accessible free of charge and open

section.title: source under a similar LGPL license. Demonstrations on how to access and use CASM’s NMR

question.text: extensions (and conditions under which they can use and modify the code) will be uploaded to the

json.answer: CASM software website: https://prisms-center.github.io/CASMcode_docs/.

section.title: Policies and provisions for re-use, re-distribution, and production of derivatives

question.text: All data will be stored in Dryad and will be available under a public domain, creative commons

json.answer: license (CC0). Note that while a personal ORCID is needed to deposit data in Dryad, no ORCID is

section.title: required to search, find and download datasets.

question.text: The existing open source software infrastructure within CASM that serves as a foundation to this

json.answer: project, is already licensed by the Regents of the University of California under the ``LGPL'' open

section.title: source license, and distributed via the prisms-center conda channel, permitting non-exclusive use of

question.text: the software. Additions to CASM will be released as LGPL to follow the current licensing of

json.answer: CASM.

section.title: Archiving of Data, Samples, and Other Relevant Research Products

question.text: Laboratory notebooks and samples will be retained for a minimum of 5 years following the

json.answer: conclusion of the program and will remain the property of UC Santa Barbara and kept on campus

section.title: after students graduate. All digital data produced over the course of the project and stored on Box

question.text: will be moved to Dryad after completion of the project for indefinite storage (>5 years).
